title: Conformance expectation
description: What one corpus entry must produce. A validate entry expects a sorted diagnostic array; an execute entry expects an ordered trace. Both carry the exit code, because a binding that finds the right problems and then exits 0 has not conformed. Message text is never expected: codes, positions, phases, actions and statuses are the contract (diagnostics.md).

kind.description: validate runs the entry through the validator and compares diagnostics. execute runs it through the runner and compares the trace.

suite.description: The suite file this expectation is for, relative to the conformance root, with forward slashes.

description.description: What this entry is for, in one sentence. Read by a person, not compared.

exitCode.description: 0 clean or warnings only, 1 a case failed, 2 a validation error or a harness error. Exit 1 is never a validate result.

strict.description: validate only: run the validator with warnings promoted to errors.

bindingCheck.description: validate only: run the validator with the portability check on, which is what reports E201.

binding.description: validate only: which binding the portability check is made against. Only meaningful with bindingCheck.

catalogOverlay.description: validate only: a corpus file whose actions are merged over the committed action catalog before the entry is validated, so that a rule the catalog drives can be proved without changing the catalog every binding ships. Relative to the conformance root.

params.description: Parameter overrides the run is given, as name to value, in the form the --param flag takes. A validate entry uses them to prove E210 for a parameter the suite does not declare.

tags.description: execute only: the tag filter the runner is given, in the same comma-separated form the command line takes. Absent means no filter.

names.description: execute only: the name filter (--name) the runner is given, as comma-separated globs in the form the command line takes. Absent means no filter.

schemaRoot.description: The schema folder the entry is validated or run against, relative to the conformance root, instead of the manifest's schemaRoot.

maxSeconds.description: execute only: the wall clock the entry must finish inside. A cancellation fixture is only proved by finishing quickly, so this is an assertion rather than a note.

diagnostics.description: validate only: every finding the validator must report, sorted by line, then column, then code. The whole set, not a sample: a binding that reports one extra finding has not conformed either.

trace.description: execute only: every entry the run must emit, in order.

diagnostic.description: One expected finding. The same shape as diagnostic.schema.json minus the file, which the entry already names, and minus the message and the suggestion, which are not part of the contract.

severity.description: error fails the validation; warning fails it only under strict.

line.description: One-based line of the offending node.

column.description: One-based column of the same node.

file.description: Only for a finding in a file other than the entry's own suite, such as a library it imports. Relative to the conformance root, with forward slashes.

traceEntry.description: One thing the runner did, in the order it did it. A trace is what makes hook order, tag selection, cancellation and row order checkable without a lab.

phase.description: Where in the run this happened. The eight execution phases in the order they can occur, plus case, which carries the result the report will show.

case.description: The case this entry belongs to. Absent for a suite-level hook, which runs outside every case.

step.description: What the runner calls this step: the Gherkin sentence when it has one, the provenance when it came from a meta step, and the row when it came from a table. Absent on a case entry.

action.description: The action the step called. Absent on a case entry.

status.description: passed, failed, skipped for something not selected or not reached, and error for a case that could not run at all.

reason.description: Why, for anything that is not passed. A closed list so that four bindings categorise a failure the same way, or a diagnostic code when one applies.
